neighbours.label: The word money in monetary economics prose
fire: When interest rates fall, households may hold more money.
The central bank increased the supply of money during the recession.
Investors moved their money from bank deposits into government bonds.
The textbook explains why demand for money rises with national income.
Inflation reduces the purchasing power of money over time.
Commercial banks create money when they extend new loans.
The analyst compared the cost of borrowing money across several markets.
A shortage of money can force firms to postpone planned investments.
quiet: When interest rates fall, households may hold more cash.
The central bank increased the supply of currency during the recession.
Investors moved their funds from bank deposits into government bonds.
The textbook explains why demand for cash rises with national income.
Inflation reduces the purchasing power of currency over time.
Commercial banks create credit when they extend new loans.
The analyst compared the cost of borrowing funds across several markets.
A shortage of cash can force firms to postpone planned investments.

notes: Three card peaks are money in economics contexts; other peaks involve tRNA and genetic carriers. This tests one lexical-contextual trigger without claiming a unitary meaning. Controls retain economics using cash, currency or funds. Codex-authored; cards only.
